evals.prompt: Create a reference implementation for merging intervals. It should be canonical, easy to audit, and include tests for edge cases.
evals.expected_output: Uses a compact semantic contract, one-owner rule mapping, behavior-first tests, and avoids fake abstractions or ceremonial artifacts.
expectations: The answer defines interval semantics and boundary behavior before implementation details.
Important semantic rules have one authoritative owner; any repeated enforcement is deliberate, traceable, and tested for agreement.
The implementation avoids abstractions that only add shape.
Does not require a canvas or phase breakdown when the implementation is already easy to reason about directly.
Tests cover golden examples, edge cases, and ordering/tie behavior.
Reports the contract, any changed behavior, and checks actually run; does not require a separate review pass after implementation.

evals.prompt: Audit the attached parser and behavior tests and decide whether it deserves to be the reference implementation. Cite file and line evidence.
evals.expected_output: A fixture-backed audit that checks semantic clarity, authoritative rule ownership, traceability, tests, and abstraction rent.
expectations: Evaluates correctness and distinguishes an authoritative rule definition from deliberate enforcement at separate boundaries.
Flags hidden assumptions and missing behavior tests.
Rejects reference status if evidence is insufficient.
Provides concrete remediation only for evidence-backed gaps.

evals.prompt: Compare the attached before and after parser implementations and their tests for hidden semantic drift. Cite the exact evidence.
evals.expected_output: A fixture-backed semantic-drift review comparing behavior rules rather than only code shape.
expectations: Compares new behavior against named reference rules.
Flags drift even if tests still pass superficially.
Distinguishes evidenced preservation from semantic changes; a move, rename, or formatting change is not behavior-preserving by definition.
Recommends targeted tests for drift cases.

evals.prompt: Audit a canonical Flutter renderer refactor that now follows this path: assured JSON map -> map-backed extension-type view -> field-for-field presentation object -> one-use build helper -> widget. The tests pass and the wire behavior is unchanged. Decide whether this deserves to be the reference implementation.
evals.expected_output: A reference-quality audit that traces the complete implementation path and requires each representation and call hop to own distinct meaning.
expectations: Preserves the assurance boundary and behavior-level tests rather than optimizing only for line count.
Traces representative callers to the widget instead of reviewing each declaration in isolation.
Flags a same-shape conversion or forwarding helper when it owns no semantics, invariant, ownership, lifecycle, or authority.
Treats a single caller as inspection evidence rather than an automatic deletion rule.
Separates implementation-shape drift from wire or behavioral drift.

evals.prompt: This attached parser is already the intended canonical version. One port rule is defined in _parseAndValidatePort and enforced independently at the decodeConfig runtime boundary and the StoredConfig.fromJson persistence boundary. Decide whether it deserves to remain the reference implementation, needs redesign, or needs a canvas. Cite file and line evidence.
evals.expected_output: Keeps the shared port rule and its two independent enforcement sites; does not demand a canvas or a single-layer redesign.
expectations: Does not require a canvas or ceremonial notes for this already-clear canonical parser.
Treats _parseAndValidatePort as the single authoritative port definition used by both decodeConfig and StoredConfig.fromJson.
Treats those two call sites as legitimate independent enforcement at runtime and persistence boundaries, not competing definitions.
Does not collapse the runtime and persistence call sites into a single validation layer.

evals.prompt: Audit whether the attached tag parser deserves to be the reference implementation. The spec never says whether duplicate tags are an error, last-wins, or first-wins. The current code silently keeps the first occurrence. Do not invent a policy. Cite what you can and cannot verify.
evals.expected_output: Surfaces the missing duplicate-tag policy, marks first-wins as unverified rather than canonical, and does not invent or rubber-stamp the contract.
expectations: Surfaces the missing duplicate-tag policy instead of inventing error, last-wins, or first-wins as canon.
Does not mark the silent first-occurrence behavior as a verified contract.
Labels any assumed duplicate rule as provisional or asks only if that decision would change the outcome.
Distinguishes any demonstrated defect from inability to establish reference quality because material policy is missing.
